oracle.scope: 6.k.W incrementally captures the explicit declared input set into immutable hash-addressed bytes. Progress is detached data; only guarded complete files can be materialized and the declared-set manifest is sealed last. Source errors preserve prior bytes, identify the logical resource, do not count the failed unit and do not trigger retry. Tests measure actual read offsets and limits, reuse captured files before the entire set, and roundtrip the completed input bytes through the existing inert Work codec. model_root_sha256 remains null, atomic_project_snapshot and durable_checkpoint remain false. Whole-project closure, writer/overarching consistency, cross-process persistence/resume and bounded total storage are not yet claimed. 6.k.R holds the existing native root-inode writer mutexes read-only across live capture, deduplicates physical source roots, and checks shallow operational state before reading and sealing. Active native guards, orphan owner records, unresolved transactions and unknown operational entries block confirmation. Every declared source is revalidated at closure; changed metadata triggers one bounded blockwise content rehash, and only hash-identical source bytes may confirm the previous binding. Changed content, missing files, unsafe paths or later observed changes retain prior captured bytes and invalidate the whole-set seal with a logical resource error. Unchanged captured prefixes are not reread per work window. Real child processes verify writer exclusion, release on seal/close/error, and fork ownership. Native guard and I/O fault injections are explicit. The scope remains an in-memory caller-declared input set: no atomic external filesystem snapshot, complete normative model closure, durable generation or cross-process resume is asserted. 6.k.C extracts the identical logical manifest and detached progress projections into a pure data module. Root paths, descriptors, native mutexes, process ownership and active hash objects stay in the runtime adapter. Structural inlining preserves the existing expressions; all W/R tests, data fields, content hashes, errors and operational boundaries remain unchanged. No additional requirement completion is inferred.

open_items: Complete project/command input closure, durable object storage, checkpoint publication, imported-state validation, reconstruction/resume and command-level missing-payload diagnostics remain future plan work. Native cooperating-writer exclusion and live declared-source closure are covered; no atomic external filesystem snapshot, Code 8 or complete requirement satisfaction is claimed.
